extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in arithmetic geometry and anabelian/IUT theory (readers familiar with Hodge theatres, prime-strips, Kummer theory and Mochizuki's IUT framework)
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of the technical structural/compatibility criteria used in IUT-style constructions: coricity (vertical/horizontal), bi-coricity of prime-strips, Kummer isomorphisms and compatibilities, multiradiality/radial algorithm properties, and local tensor/ integral structures. Focused on theta-monoid/Kummer aspects and algorithmic constructions (radial/multiradial/packets).

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertical Coricity
rubrics_metrics.description: The vertical arrows of the Gaussian log-theta-lattice induce the full poly-isomorphisms between the associated D- (cid:2) (cid:1)-Hodge theatres (where n is fixed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As stated in Theorem 12.5(1): the vertical arrows give full poly-isomorphisms n;mD(cid:31) ! n;mHT D-(cid:2)(cid:1) and n;m+1HT D-(cid:2)(cid:1). See Remark 12.3.1 for the fact that n is fixed. These vertical-induced isomorphisms are used to identify D-prime-strips and to transport structures compatibly (they are 'full poly' isomorphisms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Horizontal Coricity
rubrics_metrics.description: The horizontal arrows of the Gaussian log-theta-lattice induce the full poly-isomorphisms between the associated F ‘(cid:2)(cid:22)-prime-strips (where m is fixed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As stated in Theorem 12.5(2): horizontal arrows give full poly-isomorphisms n;mF ‘(cid:2)(cid:22) ! n+1;mF ‘(cid:2)(cid:22) etc., compatible with Corollary 11.24(4). These horizontal poly-isomorphisms identify F‘-prime-strips across horizontal shifts and are the horizontal analogue of vertical coricity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bi-coric F ‘(cid:2)(cid:22)-Prime-strips
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification and construction of F‘-prime-strips that are coric both horizontally and vertically (i.e., bi-coric).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theorem 12.5(3) explains how, via identification of collections (cid:9)cns(...) and functorial algorithms (Corollary 11.20 / 11.21), one constructs F‘-prime-strips F‘(cid:2)(cid:22)(n;mD(cid:31)) that admit poly-isomorphisms induced by both vertical and horizontal arrows. Key points: use of cns-constructed identification isomorphisms, possible non-scheme-theoretic automorphisms of absolute Galois groups produce differences in sets of isomorphisms, and composing the induced isomorphisms yields full poly-isomorphisms showing bi-coricity. Compatibility with Kummer isomorphisms is noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bi-coric Mono-analytic Log-shells
rubrics_metrics.description: The poly-isomorphisms arising from bi-coricity induce poly-isomorphisms between the associated mono-analytic log objects (log-shells / log of prime-strips).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theorem 12.5(4) gives explicit poly-isomorphisms between In;mD‘ (cid:26) log(n;mD‘) and analogous logs for F‘-prime-strips; these are compatible with the natural poly-isomorphisms and with Kummer-induced identifications (cf. Proposition 12.2(4) and Definition 12.1(1)). The log-level identifications are required to commute with the poly-isomorphisms induced at the prime-strip level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bi-coric Mono-analytic Global Realised Frobenioids
rubrics_metrics.description: The poly-isomorphisms (vertical and horizontal) induce isomorphisms of global realised Frobenioid-type triples attached to D‘-prime-strips, compatible with R>0-orbits and the functorial algorithms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theorem 12.5(5): combining (1) and (2) produces isomorphisms between triples Prime(D(...)) and associated V; fn;m(...) collections; these isomorphisms are compatible with the horizontal arrows and with the functorial algorithms of Corollary 11.21(2) and Corollary 11.24. Essentially: global Frobenioid-like structures attached to D‘-prime-strips must be preserved under the full poly-isomorphisms coming from the log-theta-lattice.

rubrics_metrics.description: There is a functorial algorithm constructing Kummer isomorphisms between D-type env data and F-type env data; these isomorphisms are compatible with Prime bijections and localisation.

The resp’d/ non-resp’d distinctions and compatibilities with Prime((cid:0)) and localisation are emphasized; the F‘-prime-strip interpretation of the env-collection is given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural homomorphisms and Kummer compatibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Natural homomorphisms from automorphism groups of F-(cid:13)-prime-strips to automorphism groups of their associated I(cid:2)(cid:22)- and F‘(cid:2)(cid:22)-prime-strips, compatible with Kummer isomorphisms; some maps are surjective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theorem 12.7(1) states the existence of homomorphisms AutF(cid:13)(F(cid:13)env(yD>)) -> AutF(cid:13)I(cid:2)(cid:22)(...) and similarly for yF env; the second homomorphisms in each line are surjective. These maps are compatible with Kummer isomorphisms of Proposition 12.6(2) and Theorem 12.5(3). Such compatibilities are necessary when transporting automorphism data across the various prime-strip realizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kummer Aspects of Multiradiality at Bad Primes
rubrics_metrics.description: At primes v in Vbad, one isolates submonoids/subgroups arising from splittings (generated by certain torsion or '1'-type elements), and these fit into a commutative diagram compatible with poly-isomorphisms and various group actions; certain composites are zero maps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theorem 12.7(2) introduces notation 1(cid:9)?env(yD>)v etc. for submonoids corresponding to splittings and torsion subgroups, and provides a large commutative diagram (involving env, Fenv, cns, Kum, and group actions Gv(M(...))) compatible with poly-isomorphisms of Corollary 11.21(2). It asserts various composites equal the zero map and that identity automorphisms are compatible with induced automorphism collections. This captures Kummer-theoretic constraints at bad primes and how they interact with multiradial structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiradiality (radial algorithm fullness)
rubrics_metrics.description: The radial algorithm (assignment from radial data to coric data) defines a functor which is full and essentially surjective; hence the radial environment is multiradial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corollary 12.8(1) defines radial datum yR = (yHT D-(...), F(cid:13)env(yD>), yRbad, F'(cid:2)(cid:22)(yD'), F'(cid:2)(cid:22)env(yD>)). The radial algorithm maps yR to a coric datum yC and on morphisms by the induced MorR. The key criterion: this functor is full and essentially surjective (i.e., every coric datum arises and morphisms lift), which is the definition used for 'multiradial'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Etale Picture of Multiradial Theta Monoids
rubrics_metrics.description: For each D-Hodge theatre one associates a radial datum; vertical and horizontal poly-isomorphisms of the Gaussian log-theta-lattice induce poly-isomorphisms of radial data, leading to identifications n;mR ~ n;m+1R and coric data n;◦C and n;◦C identified along shifts; the etale-picture admits permutation symmetry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corollary 12.8(2) explains how to construct n;mR from n;mHT D-(...) and to identify radial data across vertical/horizontal shifts using poly-isomorphisms from Theorem 12.5. The etale-picture is described (diagrammatic/visual), noting permutation symmetry and compatibility with Deﬁnition 11.24.1. This is a criterion for how local Hodge-theatre data organize into the global multiradial/etale picture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kummer Compatibility of F ‘(cid:2)(cid:22)-prime-strips (env compatibilities)
rubrics_metrics.description: Poly-isomorphisms among F‘-prime-strips induced by env / gau-Link constructions are compatible with the Kummer isomorphisms n;mF etc.; explicit commutative diagrams are provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corollary 12.8(3) states that the poly-isomorphisms obtained from env (and (env)(cid:1))(cid:19)et MorR etc.) commute with Kummer isomorphisms n;mF -> n+1;mF' and analogous objects; commutative diagrams exhibit these compatibilities. This is required when transporting F‘-level structures across the multiradial identifications without breaking Kummer compatibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kummer Compatibility of env(n+1;mD>), n;mRbad with poly-isomorphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Isomorphisms on env-level, bad-radical parts (Rbad), and associated F(cid:13)-env maps are compatible with the horizontal poly-isomorphisms (n;mF) arising from Gaussian log-theta-lattice and with Kummer isomorphisms induced by Kum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corollary 12.8(4) explains detailed compatibilities among env(n;mD>), n;mRbad, F(cid:13)env(n;mD>) and the Kummer-induced maps to V; fn;m(...) collections. Compatibility references include Proposition 12.6(2), Theorem 12.5(3,5), and Proposition 11.15; the criterion is that all these structures and maps commute in the specified manner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theta vs NF: similarities of multiradial evaluations and cyclotomic rigidity
rubrics_metrics.description: Theta functions are multiradial in two-dimensional geometric containers, using cyclotomic rigidity via (cid:22)-portion (not LCFT), and theta value evaluations use elliptic cuspidalisation; NF case uses different '1'-portion via Q>0\bZ and Belyi cuspidalisation; both have non-interference properties but different technical sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remark 12.8.1 lists similarities: multiradiality of theta functions, use of cyclotomic rigidity of mono-theta environments, and crucial non-interference property by constant multiple rigidity. NF analogues use Q>0\bZ (= {1})-portion cyclotomic rigidity and Belyi cuspidalisation. The remark describes how the evaluation methods and rigidity sources differ while both ensuring non-interference for the log-Kummer correspondence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theta vs NF: differences (local vs global, valuations, transcendental vs algebraic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Theta case: transcendental, local, compatible with profinite topology, 'one valuation' (order of zero at each cusp = 1). NF case: algebraic, global, incompatible with profinite topology, 'many valuations'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remark 12.8.1 emphasizes that theta functions are local and transcendental (order of zero = 1 at cusps), yielding cyclotomic rigidity compatible with profinite topology; NF case uses algebraic rational functions, global phenomena, and sacrifices compatibility with profinite topology (many valuations phenomenon). These characteristics are used to decide which techniques (elliptic cuspidalisation vs Belyi cuspidalisation) apply and what invariances hold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control of 'vicious circles' / indeterminacy via Iord
rubrics_metrics.description: In constructing cyclotomic rigidity isomorphisms associated to rational functions, indeterminacies arise from multiplication by orders of zeroes/poles (Iord); in theta case Iord = {1} so no extra indeterminacy, while in NF case Im(Iord -> N(cid:21)1) = {1} arising from Q>0\bZ = {1}; the final multiradial algorithm must handle Im(Iord -> f(cid:6)1g) indeterminacies but these are harmless for the totality F(cid:2)mod.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remark 12.8.1 explains the possible loops when identifying Frobenius-like Fr cyclotomes and etale-like (cid:22)8(cid:19)et via cyclotomic rigidity isomorphisms: identification may differ by multiplication by cusp-order integers. The text prescribes that in theta case Iord = {1}; in NF case Im(Iord) = {1}; and that the final algorithm tolerates the finite indeterminacy because total multiplicative structures are invariant under f(cid:6)1g. This is a criterion for acceptable levels of ambiguity in cyclotome identifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of infinite chain of log-links to recover additive structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the square involving log-links and N-th power operations is non-commutative (log(a^N) != (log a)^N), one considers an infinite chain of log-links which is invariant under vertical shift; this infinite chain can be described on one side in terms of the other, thereby enabling recovery/description of additive structure from multiplicative data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 13 explains the methodological criterion: overcome the non-commutativity obstruction by passing to the infinite chain ... -> log -> log -> log -> ... which is invariant under vertical shift. This invariance allows one to describe the infinite chain of log-links on the left-hand side via the right-hand side, a key idea in multiradial representation algorithms to 'see' additive structure from multiplicative (LGP) links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processions (n-procession) as a device to reduce indeterminacy
rubrics_metrics.description: An n-procession in a category C is a chain of capsules Pn with all capsule-full poly-morphisms; morphisms of processions are order-preserving injections together with capsule-full poly-morphisms between corresponding capsules. Using processions reduces label indeterminacies and improves constants in height inequalities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition 13.1 and Remark 13.1.1: processions allow one to send collections f1g -> f1,2g -> ... -> f1,...,l>g while reducing the (l>)^{l>} label indeterminacies to (l>)!; the reduction directly tightens coefficient factors in final height inequalities (e.g., reducing a factor from 2 to 1 in certain estimates). This is a criterion for organizing capsules to control combinatorial indeterminacy in later inequalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local Holomorphic Tensor Packets — Ring Structures
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a j-capsule of F-prime-strips indexed by S_j, the 1-tensor packet assignment VQ -> ⊕_{v|vQ} log((cid:11)F_v) and the j-tensor packet VQ -> ⊗_{(cid:11)∈S_j} log((cid:11)F_vQ) carry natural ind-topological ring structures determined by the ind-topological field structures on the summands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition 13.3(1) defines 1- and j-tensor packets as inductive limit constructions of finite-dim topological modules over Q_{vQ}; the existing ind-topological field structures on each log((cid:11)F_v) induce an ind-topological ring structure on the tensor packet, compatible with the natural action of (cid:11)(cid:5)_v on summands. This is a criterion for how local log-objects assemble into ringed tensor packets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local Holomorphic Tensor Packets — Integral Structures
rubrics_metrics.description: Integral structures on each log((cid:11)F_v) determine integral structures on the tensor packets; certain ind-topological submodules form direct summands and one obtains natural injective homomorphisms embedding lower-level tensor objects into higher-level ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition 13.3(2) constructs submodules log(S_j+1;(cid:11)F_v) as direct summands and shows injective ring homomorphisms log(S_j+1 F_vQ) <- log((cid:11)F_v) by tensoring with 1's in the omitted factors; the integral structures (cid:9)log(...) produce compatible integral structures on each direct summand appearing in the inductive limit descriptions. Use of these integral structures underlies arithmetic control in packet constructions.
